@pfarkya you have to write your commit message according to this guide https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/doc/guides/contributing/pull-requests.md#commit-message-guidelines.
This needs a test. Look at existing tests to find a good model, and use https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/doc/guides/writing-tests.md if you get stuck.
@nodejs/url
@nodejs/collaborators This could use some reviews.

Should we support the kind of this url: "http://unix:/my.socket:/main" at core, is this a standard way to define the http URL over unix socket? 

CURL treats the unix socket path and http path as different options, moreover the thing to fix #30002 should make the `url.format` and `url.parse` be reversible.

@yorkie 
> If we were to support parsing http over unix socket, I'd prefer adding a new field socketPath instead of replacing values at the host and port, which make sense for TCP only.

Good suggestion.

> moreover the thing to fix #30002 should make the url.format and url.parse be reversible.

That was my initial thought but as per my requirement I want to support `parsing http over unix socket`. Might because of that the solution diverted. We already supporting request for unix socket domain as mention here https://nodejs.org/api/http.html#http_http_request_url_options_callback.
For the fixes We need to make format and parse with same validation so that it will reversible.

Shall you help me to solve one of the above thing?

Can I just make a side comment about the title of this PR?

The title is not so helpful because it forces the reader to make both physical and mental context switches before they can decide if this PR is of interest to them.  The physical switch is that they need to follow that URL to see what that issue covers and the mental switch is that they need to read that issue and then hit the browser back button to return to this page.

What is even worse is that if you scroll to the top of this page and click on the title then you will not be transferred to the issue in question.  You have to copy the URL text, paste it into your browser's URL bar, and hit return.

A better title would be something like `make url.format and url.parser deliver reversible results`  The reader knows right away if this PR is of interest.  No context switch required.  The first line of the PR body should be `Fixes: #30002`  serves several purposes:
1. Reader's can hover over the #30002 and see the title, date, and labels of the issue
2. Readers can click on the #30002 to read the issue
3. Readers can option click on the #30002 to open the issue in a new browser tab or window
4. GitHub processes the `Fixes:` text so when this PR is merged, #30002 is automagicly closed.
@cclaus Fwiw, the commit message has been updated because of that. You should feel free to just update the PR title in cases like this.

> We already supporting request for unix socket domain as mention here https://nodejs.org/api/http.html#http_http_request_url_options_callback.

@pfarkya what you did mention here is the `socketPath` in 2nd argument, which is not the URL. Anyway, what this PR is trying to add is not covered by our docs,

- if we were to support representing unix socket with `port`, [api/url.html#url_url_port](https://nodejs.org/api/url.html#url_url_port) should be modified.
- if we were to add extra `socketPath` field, the URL doc should be updated, too.

The same question once again, do we really want this land on core? the [URL spec](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/) seems not cover any about the unix socket related, and we also have to make some API changes for their consistence.
Based on my understanding, this violates [section 3.2.2 and 3.2.3 of RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-3.2.2)

Note that the WhatWG URL standard simply drops the (invalid) colon:

```javascript
new URL('http://unix:/my.socket:/main').toString() === "http://unix/my.socket:/main"
```

@yorkie 
> The same question once again, do we really want this land on core? the URL spec seems not cover any about the unix socket related, and we also have to make some API changes for their consistence.

Yes because landing it will be helpfull for the movement toward monolith to microservice architecture.
Yes we might need some changes towards documentation, which might I need help from you all.

@tniessen Yes your concerns are valid, better we will include `unix socket over http` in URL specification which is good to have
> landing it will be helpfull for the movement toward monolith to microservice architecture i.e If some monolith application seperated in process and communicate via socket(If uses url) it would be very easy to make process as microservice and IPC communication as Network communication.

> Making my -1 explicit since this has been approved.

I also recommend it but there is different variation in different frameworks as you said(might be I am unaware of other framework specs) as of now we(node) is behind for it. If it is documented we can ask them to use the same as standard.

> Yes your concerns are valid, better we will include `unix socket over http` in URL specification which is good to have

I am not sure which URL specification you mean, but either way, that is not up to Node.js.

> landing it will be helpfull for the movement toward monolith to microservice architecture i.e If some monolith application seperated in process and communicate via socket(If uses url) it would be very easy to make process as microservice and IPC communication as Network communication.

I understand the purpose of domain sockets, but I am very much against changing the legacy `url` implementation in a way that violates the existing [URI RFC](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986) and that is incompatible with the [WhatWG URL standard](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/).

On a side note, using a different protocol such as `http+unix` seems like a better option to me than abusing malformed URLs.

@tniessen 
> I am not sure which URL specification you mean, but either way, that is not up to Node.js.

Can't we propose this need to WhatWG URL standard/URI RFC, so that new draft will include this also?

> On a side note, using a different protocol such as http+unix seems like a better option to me than abusing malformed URLs.

I am also with the same favor. But an existing uses of `unix socket over http` is https://www.npmjs.com/package/request#unix-domain-sockets which might need to be informed about these changes.

> Can't we propose this need to WhatWG URL standard/URI RFC, so that new draft will include this also?

You can try that, but the URI RFC has not been updated in more than 14 years, and I'd be surprised if there were more drafts planned. WhatWG probably doesn't want to violate that RFC.

> I am also with the same favor. But an existing uses of unix socket over http is https://www.npmjs.com/package/request#unix-domain-sockets which might need to be informed about these changes.

It's reasonable that the `request` package owns this feature support, it doesn't specify any RFC that implemented, hence it could define any rule not standard, however at the Node.js core `url` module, we should be care to add the feature support which is could be also achieved at ecosystem.

I don't see any way to implement this in Node.js without breaking existing code and violating existing standards in a dangerous way.

Closing based on feedback and inactivity, feel free to reopen @pfarkya.

issue_context.body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting a possible bug in Node.js.

Please fill in as much of the template below as you can.

Version: output of `node -v`
Platform: output of `uname -a` (UNIX), or version and 32 or 64-bit (Windows)
Subsystem: if known, please specify the affected core module name

If possible, please provide code that demonstrates the problem, keeping it as
simple and free of external dependencies as you can.
-->

* **Version**: 10.16.0
* **Platform**: 18.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 18.6.0: Thu Apr 25 23:16:27 PDT 2019; root:xnu-4903.261.4~2/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64
* **Subsystem**: url

<!-- Please provide more details below this comment. -->
The UNIX Socket domain resolution is not proper by url.parse

```
const url = require('url')
console.log(url.parse(url.format({protocol:'http', hostname:'unix', port:'/socketfile:', pathname:'/main'})))
```

expected result should be
```
Url {
  protocol: 'http:',
  slashes: true,
  auth: null,
  host: 'unix',
  port: '/socketfile',
  hostname: 'unix',
  hash: null,
  search: null,
  query: null,
  pathname: '/main',
  path: '/socketfile',
  href: 'http://unix/socketfile' }
```

but the result is 
```
Url {
  protocol: 'http:',
  slashes: true,
  auth: null,
  host: 'unix',
  port: null,
  hostname: 'unix',
  hash: null,
  search: null,
  query: null,
  pathname: '/socketfile',
  path: '/socketfile',
  href: 'http://unix/socketfile' }
```

So either we can consider it as socket URL parser and format bug or require new feature to support unix sockets URL parsing and formatting
comments: able to recreate the issue. without digging into too much details, the bug is evident, so labelling so.
Will I help to solve it ?

> Will I help to solve it ?

@pfarkya - did you mean:

 - shall I help to resolve it?

or 
 - will I get help to resolve it?

I assume it is the first one, but pls confirm.
@pfarkya - thanks for the offer to help, and welcome, please go ahead!

Removing the `confirmed-bug` label since this does not appear to be a valid URI or URL according to RFC3986, or any other standard. In particular, this will also not be compatible with the WhatWG URL specification.

> url.format and url.parser not giving reversible result

This still be valid if we drop https://www.npmjs.com/package/request#unix-domain-sockets
@pfarkya I am sorry, I do not understand your comment.

```
console.log(url.parse(url.format({protocol:'http', hostname:'xyz', port:'abc:', pathname:'/main'})))
```
output of which
```
Url {
  protocol: 'http:',
  slashes: true,
  auth: null,
  host: 'xyz',
  port: null,
  hostname: 'xyz',
  hash: null,
  search: null,
  query: null,
  pathname: '/:abc/main',
  path: '/:abc/main',
  href: 'http://xyz/:abc/main' }
```
which makes true 
`url.format and url.parser not giving reversible result` So its not about unix socket(which make voilation for URL specification).
invalid urls are not guaranteed to be reversible, regardless of the occurrence of "unix" within them.

> which makes true `url.format and url.parser not giving reversible result`

It is giving a non-"reversible result" because *your* input is invalid: `abc:` is not a valid port!

> So its not about unix socket(which make voilation for URL specification).

You are right, it is not about unix sockets, it is about *invalid* URLs. Neither unix sockets nor your example are valid URLs.

> It is giving a non-"reversible result" because your input is invalid: abc: is not a valid port!

Yes that's why `format` requires some validation so that it can't generate invalid url so that never parsing of that will cause any changes.

Given that `url.parse()` is Legacy status, the URL described here will not work with WHATWG URL, the long dormancy of this issue, and that the URL seems invalid, I'm going to close this one. Thanks, everyone.

review_comments: Document `socketPath` is needed, and I'm -1 on this name `socketPath`, it can't get which socket type is, how about `unixSocketPath`?

But `socketPath <string> Unix Domain Socket (cannot be used if one of host or port is specified, those specify a TCP Socket).`
Already has been specified `socketPath` as `Unix Domain Socket` here https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v13.x/docs/api/http.html#http_http_request_url_options_callback
But this PR has changed the returned object, and it's not internal. That's the reason that I'm -1 on adding this feature to `url` which makes confusion between them.
Should cover the above exceptions at unit tests, either?
